summary.text: Will Barclay was first elected to the New York State Assembly on November 5, 2002, and represents the 120th Assembly District, which includes Oswego County and parts of Cayuga and Jefferson Counties.
His official biography says he was elected unanimously as Leader of the Assembly Minority Conference in January 2020.

paragraphs.text: Barclay was born in Syracuse and represents the eighth generation of his family living in Pulaski, according to his Assembly biography.
He graduated from St. Lawrence University and Syracuse University College of Law, then clerked for Judge Roger J. Miner of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit.
He is a partner in the Syracuse law firm Barclay Damon, LLP, where he specializes in business law.
In the Assembly he has been Ranking Minority Member on Ways and Means, Deputy Minority Leader, Assistant Minority Leader, and Chair of the Minority Joint Conference Committee.
He and his wife, Margaret, have two sons.
